answer: Each identity escrows bonded collateral and signs cipher-bound consensus messages, making equivocation publicly verifiable. When evidence links k coordinated identities, correlated violations incur a quadratic penalty, O(k²), rather than independent flat fines. Asymmetric depreciation then compounds losses across the swarm: detection applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier, so splitting control among sybils is costly, not protective. A crystal-clear audit trail exposes coordination across the mesa of validators.
